title: Hero focal points, mobile layout repairs, and a personal tab mark
description:
Hero backdrops gained a mobile focal point so the subject stays clear of the headline at phone widths, and the headline itself was retuned. Alongside that, a run of copy and layout work: the Adventures body is now four paragraphs in the author's own words; the advisory offer was rewritten; the Find-me-online rows carry per-service brand marks and the whole row — icon, name and handle — answers to the hover instead of only the name; the Writing section stacks its lede under the heading and moves the newsletter link below the post list; and the backers credit reads as one line.

Three mobile bugs turned out to share one cause. PhotoRotator positions its frames `absolute; inset: 0` against a `relative` container, but the About and Adventures mobile media queries set that same element to `position: static` to cancel `sticky`. That removes it from the positioning chain, so the photographs resolved against a distant ancestor and rendered full-bleed — 390x1536 where the box was 342x428 — covering neighbouring sections. It read as three separate complaints (photos wildly zoomed, city names sitting over images, the Work section looking broken) and was one line of CSS in each file. `relative` cancels sticky and keeps the containing block.

Switching to `relative` then exposed a second bug: the `top: 96px` from the sticky rule is inert while sticky is unstuck, but on a relative box it is a real 96px nudge, which pushed the photograph down over the paragraphs below and made the About copy look like it was missing its opening line. `top: auto` clears it; all three sections now measure a 34px gap with zero overlap.

The rotating city fact sat a few pixels off its row on both desktop and mobile. `.cities` is an inline-block whose children are all absolutely positioned, so it held no in-flow text and had no baseline to align on. It now renders the longest city name hidden but in flow, which gives the span a real baseline and reserves the width from actual type rather than the previous `min-width: 8.6em` guess. That sizer became the span's first child, which broke the reduced-motion rule `.cities i:first-child` — no `<i>` matched it any more, so the fact rendered blank for anyone preferring reduced motion; `first-of-type` restores it.

The contact section is now sized around its Send note button, since every Get in touch link scrolls there and the button previously fell below the fold on a 1280x800 laptop and on phones. Section padding, field spacing, the form footer and the textarea all tightened, plus a height-based media query so short viewports compress further while roomy ones keep the looser rhythm. Send note now clears the fold from 1366x668 laptops upward and on modern phones; the 4.7-inch iPhone SE class still needs a short scroll, which the form's own content height makes unavoidable without cutting copy.

The tab mark is no longer Vercel's default triangle: an NE monogram in the wordmark's rust on the site's paper, drawn as vector strokes rather than set as text because favicons rasterise without the page's webfonts. Ink margins were measured at 16, 32 and 64px to confirm nothing clips. Shipped as icon.svg, a 32px raster fallback, a 180px apple-touch icon, and a genuine PNG-embedded favicon.ico so no legacy client gets a 404.

Extraction: NavMark and NavLinks moved out of the three-component Nav.tsx into their own files with a shared sections.ts, SocialRow and SubmitRow were pulled out of SocialList and ContactForm, and Writing's bare layout wrapper folded into WritingCta. Every affected capture came back pixel-identical, which is what proves the refactor moved structure and not pixels.
